question_bank.stem: A generator maps a low-dimensional code to a larger image. Why does this motivate deconvolution or upsampling layers?

options.text: The network must increase spatial dimensionality toward an image output
The network must reduce an image into a single class probability
The network must remove all padding before every convolution
The network must replace gradients with benchmark scores

question_bank.rationale: The lecture motivates deconvolution by noting that a generator's input is smaller than its image-shaped output.

distractor_rationales.B: That describes a classifier-like direction, not generator upsampling.
distractor_rationales.C: Padding details do not explain why spatial size must grow.
distractor_rationales.D: Benchmark scores are unrelated to deconvolutional image generation.

source_ref.evidence_span: The output is an image of more dimensions.

frame_evidence.description: Slide motivates upsampling/deconvolution with a generator mapping a smaller latent code to an image.

question_bank.stem: Rewriting a 1D convolution as matrix multiplication helps explain transposed convolution because the forward operation can be expressed as what product?

options.text: A sparse weight matrix multiplied by the input vector
A softmax vector divided by the class score
A validation curve multiplied by the learning rate
A token embedding matrix averaged over words

question_bank.rationale: The lecture explicitly rewrites conv1d as a matrix multiplication with a weight matrix times the input.

distractor_rationales.B: Softmax probabilities are not the matrix view of convolution.
distractor_rationales.C: Loss curves and learning rates are training telemetry.
distractor_rationales.D: Token embeddings are unrelated to the 1D convolution derivation.

source_ref.evidence_span: write it as a matrix multiplication.

frame_evidence.description: Slide writes a 1D convolution as a sparse matrix-vector multiplication y = Wx.

question_bank.stem: In the lecture's implementation intuition, transposed convolution can be approximated with what set of operations?

options.text: Transpose the convolution matrix, insert zeros, flip filters, and use fractional stride
Normalize the softmax, drop padding, average logits, and freeze filters
Hash the input, compare n-grams, replace labels, and retrain the head
Pool maxima, forget switches, mask classes, and erase feature maps

question_bank.rationale: The instructor describes transposing W and implementing the operation by inserting zeros, flipping filters, and using a sub-pixel stride.

distractor_rationales.B: These are not the transposed-convolution operations from the derivation.
distractor_rationales.C: Those are contamination-check steps, not a deconvolution implementation.
distractor_rationales.D: Forgetting switches would break unpooling; it is not the transposed-convolution recipe.

source_ref.evidence_span: you can actually flip the filter.

frame_evidence.description: Slide shows the transposed-convolution intuition with W transposed, flipped filters, zero insertion, and fractional stride.
